Split isStableOuter into identity and purity. A module binding used only as a JSX tag or passed as a value needs a fixed identity: no write after module load, where top-level `X.displayName = ...` and `X.defaultProps = ...` statements count as load-time, not as writes. Purity (readsChangingState) is checked only when the unit calls the binding during render, and only over the callee's eager code (walkEager/findDeferred already exist), so `ref.current` in an effect or `document` in a handler no longer marks a component unstable as a tag. This is the shape the planner was not tuned on: 7 of 8 heldout2 files carry 29 such writes against 0 in all 54 base, tuning and heldout files, and discussions_table (9 writes, 12 of its 15 refusals outer_binding_unstable) holds the largest gap to React Compiler, 42 work.

claims.text: Amend P10 to the identity side only. A module binding X is identity-stable when every member write or Object.assign(X, ...) on it is an unconditional statement at module top level (displayName, defaultProps, propTypes, compound `X.Item = Item` all count); any other member write, or X handed to a call, keeps the refusal. Purity is unchanged: a same-module component used as a tag still needs a pure eager body, memo still exempt, imports still assumed pure. P12 must report how many of the 51 heldout2 outer_binding_unstable sites fail on identity versus purity; that identity share is P10's target, and P10 ships only if it is nonzero on the development sets. Estimate about 320k (O14 calibration).

claims.why: O11 showed none of P11's named targets is blocked by isResultReadOnly (form_check's `selected` is useState, toaster_store calls a method on a destructured hook result, accordion has no gap), and O12 showed callback methods can change or keep elements.
claims.text: Make P11 conditional and narrow. It is built only if P12's weighted census attributes at least 15% of the equal-to-uncompiled steps on the development sets to non-hook cand_result_not_readonly refusals; otherwise it is dropped and its 330k is not spent. If built, rule (b) keeps only methods without callbacks that return a primitive or a fresh copy (includes, indexOf, lastIndexOf, slice, join, at, `length`), callback methods (find, map, filter, some, every) count only when the callback body passes the existing mutation check and the result's uses pass isReadOnlyUse recursively, and rule (a) (primitive-returning functions) is dropped as unproven. The toaster_store gap (29) is left to whatever family P12 names for it.

Add four P15 mutation operators: (1) for O8, make the eager body of a same-module child used only as a JSX tag read Date.now(), a changing global or ref.current during render, with and without memo; (2) for O12, a map/filter/find/some/every callback that writes a field of its element (`i.seen = true`) or pushes it to an outer array; (3) for O12, a `find` result changed after the call (`y.n++`); (4) for O10, move a top-level `X.displayName = ...` or `X.Item = Item` into a conditional, a function body or a handler. Operators (2) and (3) are needed only if P11 is built. Each P10 and P11 review round runs them on both targets and needs 0 differences.

claims.text: As written, P10 checks purity only when the unit calls the binding, so a same-module component used only as a tag (`<Clock/>`, whose render reads `Date.now()` or a changing global) would get a cached element, and React then skips Clock's render where uncompiled code re-renders it: a difference. A tag use still needs the child's eager body to be pure; only `memo` already has skip semantics (isWrapperCall's comment says so). P15's matching operator mutates only components 'the parent calls as X()', so the mutants would not catch this hole. Likely if P10 is built as worded.

evidence.source: packages/forgetti/src/next/plan/baseline.ts 323-346 (isStableOuter runs readsChangingState for every same-module function, tag or call) and 367-371 (memo exemption: 'memo(x) skips a render on equal props, as an unchanged element does'); P10 and P15 text
evidence.detail: The purity check on tags is what keeps a cached element from skipping a child whose render reads changing state; the code exempts only memo because it alone already skips on equal props. A P15 operator 'read a changing global in the eager body of a same-module child used as a JSX tag' closes the gap in the net.

claims.text: P10's purity narrowing does not exclude effects: walkEager treats any closure that is a call argument as eager, so `useEffect(() => ref.current ...)` and custom hooks such as useEventCallback stay flagged; only closures in JSX attributes (handlers) are deferred. Excluding effects needs a list of hooks known to defer their callback, and custom hooks cannot be on it. The split between identity failures (displayName) and purity failures inside the 51 outer_binding_unstable sites is also unmeasured, since T1 does not name the failing binding (J12).

evidence.source: packages/forgetti/src/next/plan/baseline.ts 157-198 (CALLS, walkEager: 'A closure written as a call argument may run during render, so it is walked'; findDeferred); J12 caveat
evidence.detail: deferred = !called && FUNCTIONS.has(type); a useEffect callback sits under a CallExpression, so called is true and its body is walked. P10's example 'ref.current in an effect no longer marks a component unstable' does not follow from reusing walkEager/findDeferred.

claims.text: Make P10's identity rule structural instead of a two-name whitelist: any assignment to a member of X that is an unconditional statement at module top level runs at load time (displayName, defaultProps, propTypes, compound `X.Item = Item`), and a top-level `Object.assign(X, {...})` counts the same; any other member write or X handed to a call keeps the refusal. Same predicate, same cost, and it covers the static-member shapes real libraries use that the flattened corpus dropped.

claims.text: P11(b) counts `x.find/map/filter/some/every` on a call result as read-only uses, but their callbacks receive x's elements and may change or keep them (`x.map(i => { i.seen = true; return i })`), and `find` returns an element that later code may change (`const y = x.find(...); y.n++`). Sound only if each callback body passes the same mutation check and the returned element's uses are checked recursively, as isReadOnlyUse already does for `x.a`. P15 has no operator for either; add both.

evidence.detail: The current rule recurses on the holder's use for every read path; a method-name whitelist without callback and result checks drops that recursion. J5/J6 record that every widening so far found a new soundness hole in review.

questions.ask: If the planner work comes back sound and within size on the new held-out set but still does more React work than React Compiler (in total or on some file), what should happen next: (a) ship the compiler as it is and record the miss, (b) allow more planner work on the old development sets only, without building another held-out set, or (c) build another held-out set and try again?
questions.answer: (a) Ship the compiler as it is, replacing forgetti 0.8, and record the React miss; planner improvements can follow in later releases.
